description:
The palace in Polanka, today a district of Krosno, is dated to the 19th century by the heritage record of the regional conservator's office; it is not known whether it was built from scratch or created by rebuilding an earlier manor house. Polanka was a noble village, and its manor was for a time associated with the Trzecieski family.

In the 20th century the palace was used by various institutions, including oil companies and workers' cooperatives. After the Second World War the plundered building was used to keep horses and cattle. In mid-2006 the palace and park complex was bought by a private investor and, after years of neglect, renovated and returned to use; it now operates as a four-star hotel with newer buildings alongside the historic palace, with an indoor swimming pool, a wellness area and breakfast included on the rate seen.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At ul. Popiełuszki 103 in the Polanka district of Krosno, Subcarpathia; Booking lists free private parking and notes train access.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €117/night for a 17 m² Standard Double Room with a full bed or two single beds, a garden view, air conditioning, a private bathroom, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast included; taxes included. Free cancellation applied before 25 November on the rate seen, with no prepayment and payment at the property. A Deluxe Room was around €135.

**On-site:** An indoor swimming pool, a wellness area with a hot tub, on-site parking and free Wi-Fi.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for a 26–27 November stay, so check your own dates on Booking. The hotel complex has the historic palace and newer buildings, so ask the hotel which one your room is in.
